feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications/platform leader, with clear specialization in public-sector web modernization, governance, analytics, and multimedia. It reads polished and substantive, but it is somewhat repetitive and could be tightened to sharpen differentiation, outcomes, and executive-level impact.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear positioning: the headline, summary, and experience align well around digital platform leadership in complex, mission-driven organizations.  
- Strong credibility: specific platforms, tools, and scale markers like “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and “50+ internal publishers” add weight.  
- Good breadth: combines strategy, technical execution, analytics, editorial systems, and multimedia in a way that supports senior leadership branding.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce repetition: “digital strategy,” “workflows,” “governance,” and “content operations” recur heavily across sections; consolidate overlapping skills/technical areas to improve scanability.  
- Add more outcome-focused results: several bullets describe responsibilities well but would be stronger with measurable business/user impact beyond scale (e.g., efficiency gains, engagement lifts, adoption improvements).  
- Minor style/consistency issues: “Coleman DAVIS” capitalization is stylistically inconsistent; punctuation around lists varies; “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; “A2/Learning” reads awkwardly. No major misspellings or grammar errors otherwise.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus, but it’s slightly dense and repeats themes already covered in the subtitle, competencies, and work experience. Tightening it will improve scanability and sharpen differentiation.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace “building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind” with more direct phrasing like “leading enterprise web platforms, governance, and content operations for.”
- Add one concrete scale signal from recent experience, e.g. “10,000+ page websites” or “high-volume public-sector organizations,” to increase specificity.
- Consider trimming the list to 3–4 priority areas most relevant to target roles: web modernization, governance, analytics, and AI-enabled experiences.
- Suggested rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience leading enterprise web platforms, governance, and content operations for high-volume public-sector organizations. Drives web modernization, analytics ecosystems, editorial systems, and AI-enabled user experiences that improve reach, usability, and operational efficiency.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences,” “analytics infrastructure,” and “editorial systems” are repeated in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- “High-volume public-sector communications” overlaps with the subtitle and multiple NACo role descriptions.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. It would be sharper if phrased as broader capability areas and trimmed to avoid repeating near-identical wording.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use slightly higher-level labels to complement, not mirror, other sections: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and content operations • Analytics, reporting and performance insights • Cross-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production
- Standardize style: use “and” instead of mixing “&” with “and” for a cleaner, more formal tone.
- Consider replacing “editorial systems” with “content operations” for broader clarity and stronger alignment with the experience section.
- “Search and content discovery” is clearer and more user-focused than “content experiences.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization” and “AI-enabled search…” repeat language from the header almost verbatim.
- Several items also duplicate Topline Skills categories, especially analytics, multimedia, and workflow automation.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and overlaps with Work Experience. Tightening phrasing, standardizing style, and emphasizing outcomes or scope will make it more distinctive and scannable.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a short intro line like “Selected recent projects” and format each item as a concise 1-line achievement with parallel structure.
- Tighten wording: “hybrid retrieval, vector search, and bill-level AI chat” is strong; cut filler like “designed for continued campaign growth.”
- Standardize style and punctuation: use sentence fragments or full sentences consistently; spell out “10-by-20-foot” for style consistency.
- Where possible, add scope or result signals (audience, campaign purpose, platform scale) to increase impact.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search and the microsite closely repeat achievements already covered in the current consultant role.
- Advocacy Video Series overlaps with the Associate Communications Director and Director of Digital Media entries; keep this footer focused on standout examples, not role summaries.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope, but it reads broad and overlaps heavily with earlier NACo entries and the Recent Projects section. Make it sharper by emphasizing consultant-level outcomes, transformation work, and what is new since returning in 2024.

Suggested edit
- Open with a tighter summary focused on advisory impact: “Advise NACo on digital strategy, content operations, Drupal platform enhancements, and enterprise web modernization as an external consultant.”
- Consolidate overlapping duties into 3–4 bullets; lead with highest-impact work: AI search initiative, campaign/microsite architecture, and org-wide workflows/analytics.
- Replace generic verbs (“build and refine,” “advise on”) with outcome-oriented phrasing: “Designed,” “Implemented,” “Standardized,” “Led.”
- Add measurable outcomes if available: number of sites/campaigns launched, workflow time reduced, search relevance gains, toolkit downloads, stakeholder teams supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance, usability, and operational best practices” repeats themes from Director of Digital Media; only keep if tied to a distinct consulting outcome.
- Microsites, AI search, and anniversary/campaign work already appear in Recent Projects; avoid repeating project detail verbatim.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize enterprise ownership and outcomes while avoiding overlap with the earlier NACo role’s newsletter/video execution details.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper scope statement: “Directed NACo’s enterprise digital communications function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Combine and streamline channel bullets; focus on leadership and scale, not routine oversight: “Oversaw website, email, and social channels serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and tens of thousands of county officials.”
- Make the website bullet more outcome-led: “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 50+ internal publishers and improving platform governance and publishing efficiency.”
- Add measurable impact where possible for analytics/studio/governance (e.g., reporting time reduced, production cost savings, engagement growth, faster publishing cycles).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Current email/social/video language overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership, modernization, and systems.
- “Governance/publishing standards/workflows” also appears in multiple NACo roles; use distinct wording or attach a concrete result here.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry reads generic and overlaps with both the later Director role and the earlier Digital Media Manager/Producer role. Tighten it around scope, channel ownership, and systems/process improvements introduced at this level.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize operational ownership: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, supporting advocacy campaigns and organization-wide editorial execution.”
- Make bullets more outcome-oriented: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders” and, if possible, add open rates, growth, or send volume.
- Clarify the video impact: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel across web, email and social.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “helped improve” with direct contribution: “Built/standardized editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving coordination and publishing consistency.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with the 2015–2018 role and Recent Projects; distinguish this entry as scaling/operationalizing the series.
- “Editorial coordination/workflows” overlaps with the 2022–2024 governance bullet; keep this version tactical, not enterprise-level.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this skills block is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo roles. It should sharpen the leadership scope and emphasize higher-value, recent strengths rather than broad communications language.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with tighter, more senior phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy & web modernization
- Editorial governance & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector advocacy communications
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Prefer “content operations” over “content planning” to better reflect systems/governance leadership shown in recent roles.
- Consider swapping “public-sector and advocacy messaging” for “stakeholder communications strategy” if you want a less tactical, more executive tone.
- Keep this section purely strategic; let platform/tool specifics stay in the technical skills sections.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” substantially repeat Core Competencies.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with the header and multiple NACo experience bullets.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill coverage, but this item is too tool-list-heavy and overlaps heavily with the separate “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, it should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and modernization themes rather than repeat software names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms • Website modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”
- Remove lower-priority or older-signal items like jQuery unless it is still central to current work.
- Put the strongest, most recent differentiators first: Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, integrations/automation.
- If space allows, sharpen with scope language: “enterprise CMS modernization” or “public-sector web platforms.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, HTML/CSS/JavaScript, API integrations, and Airtable already appear in “Technical + IT.”
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also repeats the header/core competencies; keep wording distinct or shorten here.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize strategic application and decision-making impact rather than repeat software names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as capability-led, with fewer tools: “Analytics strategy • KPI framework design • Executive and leadership reporting • User behavior and journey analysis • SEO and performance optimization”
- If you want 1–2 tools, keep only the most strategic/recent: “GA4, BigQuery” or “GA4, Looker Studio, Power BI”
- Replace “Microsoft Clarity” with a broader outcome phrase like “behavioral insights” unless Clarity is central to target roles
- Consider a tighter final version: “Analytics strategy • KPI design • Executive reporting • Behavioral and SEO performance analysis • GA4, BigQuery, Power BI”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current wording duplicates the Technical + IT “Data, Analytics & Optimization” section almost exactly
- “Leadership reporting” also overlaps with “analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads as a generic tool list and overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” elsewhere. Make it more senior, outcome-oriented, and aligned to recent studio/event leadership.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: **Multimedia Production, Studio & Event Operations**
- Replace with tighter, higher-level bullets such as:
- Broadcast-quality video production and editing  
- Livestream and hybrid event delivery  
- PTZ camera and in-house studio operations  
- Virtual event production and technical coordination
- If space allows, add one impact cue tied to recent work, e.g. “Built and operated an in-house studio supporting advocacy programming and event coverage.”
- Keep phrasing parallel and avoid mixing broad functions with narrow tools unless the tool signals real specialization.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Livestreaming” and “Hybrid and virtual event production” overlap with Core Competencies: “Multimedia production and livestream operations.”
- “Studio operations” is already supported by the Director of Digital Media bullet about building NACo’s first in-house video studio.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, scannable list, but it’s generic and slightly redundant with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Since Drupal is central to recent roles, this item should emphasize depth/recency rather than read as a flat software inventory.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance and recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages** is fine, but consider **Drupal (enterprise migrations, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**.
- Add light qualifiers only where they reinforce recent impact, e.g. **Drupal (10,000+ page migration; custom microsites)** if your format allows.
- If keeping as a pure skills line, tighten to the platforms you’ve materially used in recent work; drop any tool with limited depth.
- Consider renaming to **CMS & Web Platforms** for cleaner phrasing.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps heavily with **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; keep one broader and one more specific.
- “CMS modernization” already appears elsewhere, so don’t repeat that phrase here.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This section should feel more implementation-focused and emphasize current, higher-value tools.

Suggested edit
- Reframe from languages to applied execution: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery”
- Group modern tooling by use case: “Integrations & deployment: API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions”
- If accurate, add scope or outcomes in adjacent experience bullets instead of here, e.g., GTM/Workers used for analytics, performance, or campaign delivery
- Consider dropping version numbers unless required; “HTML, CSS, JavaScript” is cleaner and more senior

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” already appears under Topline Skills; keep the fuller phrasing in one place only
- “API integrations” and workflow automation themes also overlap with Core Competencies and Topline Skills; this section should stay strictly tool-based

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems leadership. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” and “Airtable systems” elsewhere, so tighten and position around implementation depth.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools
- Group by function for clarity: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier • Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp • Slack, Microsoft Teams
- Consider adding a qualifier if accurate: “Workflow design, no-code automation, project coordination, cross-team collaboration”
- If space allows, prioritize strongest/recent tools first: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Slack • Microsoft Teams

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating those exact phrases here.
- Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp are similar; listing all four may feel padded unless each was meaningfully used.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This is clear but too bare relative to the rest of the CV. It would be stronger if it signaled level of use and aligned more directly with the recent email/newsletter leadership described in NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- If accurate, add scope/usage context: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (campaign automation, segmentation) • Higher Logic (member email/community engagement) • Mailchimp (newsletter distribution)**
- Order by strongest/recentest platform first; if Dynamics 365 is most current, keep it first. If Higher Logic was the primary NACo tool, move it first.
- Consider adding one qualifier only if true: **enterprise email operations** or **newsletter and audience engagement systems** to better connect with work experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item overlaps with repeated email-channel references in Work Experience; avoid adding generic phrases like “email newsletters” here unless tied to platform capability.
- Don’t repeat analytics terms already covered under **Data, Analytics & Optimization**.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool list, but it overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills” and misses a chance to show level of capability. In a technical section, tighten it into clearer categories and emphasize analysis/optimization methods over generic nouns.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • SEO analysis • A/B testing • KPI/dashboard reporting**
- Put the strongest, most current platforms first: GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Clarity.
- Replace **Dashboarding** with **KPI/dashboard reporting** or **performance reporting**; it sounds more outcome-oriented and less vague.
- If space allows elsewhere, tie these tools to impact in recent roles rather than expanding this list here (e.g., analytics infrastructure, reporting for decision-making).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item is nearly identical to **Topline Skills → Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider deleting one or making this version tools-only and the Topline version capability-focused.
- “SEO” and “A/B testing” are useful, but avoid repeating optimization language already implied in core competencies and work experience.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and reads like a setup for later roles rather than a results-focused accomplishment. Tighten it to emphasize team-building, channel ownership, and concrete outputs without repeating achievements covered in 2018–2024 roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and support day-to-day operations across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Split contributions into sharper actions: website refresh, recurring video/livestream production, workflow improvement, informal supervision.
- Add metrics if available: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, email volume, traffic impact from the website refresh, or team size.
- Suggested version: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations. Contributed to a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, improved cross-channel publishing workflows, and provided day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 advocacy video bullet; differentiate by framing this as launch/early production.
- Avoid repeating broad workflow language already used in later NACo roles unless you can make it more specific.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads generic and overlaps with later multimedia/digital roles. Tighten it to emphasize cross-functional coordination and the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the strongest outcome: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy teams, and launched the organization’s first podcast from concept through scripting and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with a more specific verb: “produced” or “developed multimedia and digital content supporting program and policy communications.”
- If possible, add scope or output: number of projects supported, podcast episodes launched, audiences reached, or teams/stakeholders coordinated.
- Keep this entry shorter than later NACo roles; one concise sentence or two bullets is enough.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later Digital Media Manager / Producer and Associate Communications Director entries.
- Avoid repeating broad digital/media leadership themes already covered more strongly in 2015–2024 roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but reads more like a mix of software and capabilities. It also overlaps with “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” and several work bullets, so tighten it to tool-specific skills and keep broader production capabilities elsewhere.

Suggested edit
- Rename or refocus as software/tools only: “Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator”
